# Method of approach

This chapter answers the "how" question --- how did you complete your project,
including the overall design of your study, details of the algorithms and tools you
have used, etc. Use technical diagrams, equations, algorithms, and paragraphs of text
to describe the research that you have completed. Be sure to number all figures and
tables and to explicitly refer to them in your text.

<!--
WRITING GUIDE for Chapter Three

HTML comments are stripped from the PDF and the website; they are here for you
to read while you draft.

THE TEST OF THIS CHAPTER IS REPRODUCTION

Assume the reader is another 600-level student who has your repository and this
chapter but has never met you. Could they rerun your study and get comparable
results? If not, the chapter is missing something. Can you first and second
reader(s) study this method and see clearly that you understand all of the
technical details in this project? If not, then the chapter is missing
something that shows you did furnish sufficient the technical details.

WHAT TO COVER

Address the items that apply to your project (the syllabus expects at least five
of them): algorithms, programming languages, libraries, platforms, frameworks,
software, hardware, data, and theories. Always give versions, because versions
change behavior: "Python 3.11 and scikit-learn 1.4.0", not "Python and a machine
learning library". Record anything a reader must install or configure.

JUSTIFY, DO NOT ONLY DESCRIBE

"We used PostgreSQL" is a description. "We used PostgreSQL because the workload
is write-heavy and we needed multi-row transactions; SQLite would have been
simpler to deploy but would have serialized our concurrent writers" is a
justification. Whenever you chose between two reasonable options, say what you
chose, why, and what you gave up. Design decisions are the scientific content of
this chapter.

CONNECT TO THE REPOSITORY AND TO THE EVALUATION

Link to the artifact repository by URL, and show at least one input and the
corresponding output so that the reader can see the artifact's contract. Then
make sure every mechanism you describe here is exercised by an experiment in
Chapter Four: a component that no experiment touches is unexplained work.
-->

## Experimental Setup

## Reproducibility

List what a reader needs to reproduce the study: operating system, language and

transcribing commands that will drift out of date.
-->
